title: Yjs vs Automerge: Which One Scales? ⚡
fb_caption:
Yjs vs Automerge: Which Architecture Actually Scales in Production? ⚡

• Throughput: Yjs generally excels with higher throughput due to its CRDT-based approach and efficient binary encoding, while Automerge can face performance bottlenecks with large datasets or complex merge operations.
• Latency: Both aim for low latency, but Yjs's optimized data structures can offer more predictable performance, especially in high-concurrency scenarios.
• Consistency: Both provide strong eventual consistency. Yjs's conflict resolution is often considered more straightforward and predictable.
• Failure Modes: Yjs tends to be more robust against network partitions and concurrent edits due to its design. Automerge's history-based approach can sometimes lead to more complex merge conflicts.
• Operational Overhead: Yjs often has lower operational overhead due to its performance and simpler state management.

Recommendation: For production environments demanding high scalability, predictable performance, and robust conflict resolution, Yjs is often the preferred choice.
